A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between v1's Appendices A–D and v2's Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results for PSR, NSR, and Weighted-REINFORCE, including benchmark scores and training dynamics in Figures 2–4 and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Llama evaluations, vanilla REINFORCE scores, and reward-weight sensitivity results in Figure 4 and Tables 1 and 4.

M1.justification: PSR, NSR, and Weighted-REINFORCE retain the same objectives and procedures, including the default positive-reward weight of 0.1. Additional backbone evaluations and weight settings test the existing methods rather than introduce new components.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH and evaluate mathematical reasoning on MATH, AIME 2025, and AMC23. The added Llama backbone and reward-weight sweep do not introduce different datasets, tasks, or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds vanilla REINFORCE to all three benchmark comparisons in Table 1; the existing comparators remain. REINFORCE also appears as lambda = 1 in Table 4. Unlikelihood training is compared analytically, not evaluated as an experimental baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as an evaluated backbone, using a 4,096-token context and 256 evaluation responses per prompt. Appendix E tests lambda values 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, and 1. The retained Qwen settings, datasets, and Pass@k evaluation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a systematic sensitivity analysis of the defining reward-weight parameter, whereas v1 reports the selected weight without such a sweep. The Llama comparison also tests dependence on model family and exposes a failure of the favorable Qwen scaling behavior. These substantially extend validation of robustness and applicability.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same unbiased Pass@k estimator. Neither reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional evaluation samples and result rows do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All retained Table 1 scores and existing result plots are unchanged. New REINFORCE results include MATH Pass@1/Pass@256 of 74.8/92.0, versus the retained Weighted-REINFORCE scores of 76.6/96.7. Figure 4 adds Llama results showing degraded large-k performance after RL, and Table 4 adds weight-dependent results. These substantially expand the empirical findings.

T1.justification: New Appendix B introduces the unlikelihood objective and its token-logit gradient in Equations 10–11, formally contrasting it with NSR. The entropy derivation is relocated from Appendix A rather than newly added. Existing PSR/NSR mathematics remains equivalent despite notation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract expands its stated empirical scope from two Qwen models to include Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct while retaining the claim of consistent full-spectrum NSR improvement. The contribution bullets and conclusion otherwise retain the same claims about decomposition, prior preservation, and Weighted-REINFORCE.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the Llama results as evidence that RL benefits depend on the backbone, replacing v1's Qwen-only future-work limitation with an observed boundary. It also adds interpretations of weight sensitivity and unlikelihood gradients, and contextualizes extended-training instability as affecting other RL algorithms too.

D1.justification: v2 documents Llama's context length and evaluation sampling settings, including temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95, and specifies the reward-weight grid. Existing Qwen prompt templates, clipping and KL settings, hardware information, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Nine references are added, including Llama 3, unlikelihood training, and work on model priors and RL instability. The new unlikelihood comparison sharpens the distinction from earlier negative-learning objectives, while the broader RLVR and inference-scaling positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. v2 makes local additions, separates the entropy comparison into Appendix B, adds the weight-sensitivity appendix, and renumbers subsequent appendices. The conference footer and acknowledgments are also updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel Llama Figure 4 and ablation Table 4. Table 1 gains REINFORCE rows, changes comparator order, and revises emphasis. Existing figures are retained, with some renumbering and document reflow; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added REINFORCE control and weight ablation better substantiate reward reweighting, while the Llama experiment turns an untested generality limitation into a documented failure case. The unlikelihood derivation also clarifies the theoretical comparison. These gains are limited by incomplete integration: the abstract retains its broad improvement claim despite Figure 4, and Table 4 misidentifies some best results through highlighting—for example, MATH Pass@256 of 96.9 is bold while the higher 97.1 is not.
